title: More, less, as … as, the most
description: Compare people and things: mais and menos do que, tão quanto, melhor and maior, and the most.

guide.summary: Portuguese compares with small words around the adjective: mais … do que, menos … do que, tão … quanto. Four common adjectives have their own one-word forms, a superlative is just the article plus the comparative, and -íssimo turns very + adjective into one word. The adjective always agrees with what it describes.

sections.title: More … than: mais … do que
sections.text: Portuguese has no -er ending. Put mais before the adjective and do que before the second thing. Plain que is just as correct and very common in speech.

rows: do que eu, do que você

steps: Put mais right before the adjective.
Make the adjective agree with the first thing.
Add do que or que before the second thing.

examples.pt: O trem é mais rápido do que o ônibus.
examples.en: The train is faster than the bus.

examples.pt: Minha irmã é mais alta que eu.
examples.en: My sister is taller than me.

watch: Than is never de: mais caro de o hotel is wrong.
Muito means very and cannot be followed by do que.
After than use eu, not mim: mais alta do que eu.

sections.title: Less … than: menos … do que
sections.text: Menos works exactly like mais. Brazilians use it less than English does: they often prefer mais with the opposite adjective, but both are correct.
steps: Put menos before the adjective.
Finish with do que or que, never como.

examples.pt: O chá é menos doce do que o suco.
examples.en: The tea is less sweet than the juice.

watch: Pouco means little and does not compare.

sections.title: As … as: tão … quanto
sections.text: To say two things are equal, put tão before the adjective and quanto or como before the second thing. Tão never changes form. Não before the verb makes not as … as.
steps: Check an adjective follows: then use tão.
Finish with quanto or como.
Never use do que after tão.

examples.pt: Ana é tão alta quanto a irmã.
examples.en: Ana is as tall as her sister.

examples.pt: A sopa não está tão quente quanto o café.
examples.en: The soup is not as hot as the coffee.

watch: Tão do que is a common mix-up: do que belongs to mais and menos.
Tanto is for nouns, tão for adjectives.

sections.title: As much, as many: tanto … quanto
sections.text: Before a noun, as much or as many is tanto, and it agrees with the noun: tanto, tanta, tantos, tantas. After a verb, tanto quanto never changes.
steps: Is a noun coming? If not, use tanto quanto unchanged.
If yes, find its gender and number.
Pick tanto, tanta, tantos or tantas and finish with quanto.

examples.pt: Eu tenho tantos livros quanto você.
examples.en: I have as many books as you.
He works as much as me.

watch: Never tão before a noun: tão comida is wrong.

sections.title: Better, worse, bigger, smaller
sections.text: Four adjectives have their own one-word comparatives. They do not change for gender but add -es in the plural.
steps: Spot bom, mau, ruim, grande or pequeno.
Replace mais + adjective with the single word.
Add -es if the subject is plural.

examples.pt: Este restaurante é melhor do que aquele.
examples.en: This restaurant is better than that one.

examples.pt: Nossa casa é maior do que a sua.
examples.en: Our house is bigger than yours.

watch: Mais ruim is heard in casual speech, but pior is the form to use.
Mais pequeno is used in Portugal; Brazilians say menor.
For age, say mais velho (older) and mais novo (younger), not maior or menor.

sections.title: The most: o mais … de
sections.text: Put the article before the comparative: o mais caro, a mais bonita, o melhor. In or of after it is de + article: do, da, dos, das.

rows: o / a + noun + mais + adjective + de
o restaurante mais caro da cidade

steps: Choose o or a to match the noun.
Add mais + adjective, or use melhor, pior, maior, menor.
Join de to the article of the place or group: da cidade, do ano.

examples.pt: É o melhor restaurante da cidade.
examples.en: It is the best restaurant in the city.

examples.pt: Ana é a aluna mais inteligente da turma.
examples.en: Ana is the cleverest pupil in the class.

watch: English in becomes de: da cidade, not na cidade.
Without the article, melhor only means better.

sections.title: Very: -íssimo and ótimo
sections.text: Muito + adjective means very. The ending -íssimo says the same in one word, a little stronger: drop the final vowel and add -íssimo, -íssima. Very good is usually ótimo.
steps: Drop the last vowel of the adjective.
Add -íssimo or -íssima to match the noun.
Never put muito in front of the new word.
watch: Muito ótimo is wrong: ótimo already means very good.
The accent always falls on the í.

sections.title: The adjective still agrees
sections.text: Comparison words never change (mais, menos, tão), but the adjective agrees with the thing it describes, the subject, not the thing after do que. Melhor, pior, maior, menor take -es in the plural.
steps: Find the subject, the thing described.
Give the adjective its gender and number.
Make the verb agree too: é or são.

examples.pt: As casas são tão caras quanto o apartamento.
examples.en: The houses are as expensive as the flat.

watch: What follows do que does not decide the form.
Tão and mais never take an ending.

exercises.instruction: Keep the meaning but start with O ônibus and use menos.

exercises.feedback: If the train is faster, the bus is less fast.

answers: O ônibus é menos rápido do que o ônibus.

exercises.instruction: Fix the error.

exercises.instruction: Choose the word for as.

answers: tão
exercises.feedback: Before an adjective, as … as is tão … quanto.
exercises.explanation: Tão alta quanto a irmã: as tall as her sister. Tão never changes form.

answers: tanto

answers: mais
mistakes.why: Mais pairs with do que, not with quanto.

exercises.instruction: Choose the word that finishes as … as.

answers: de

exercises.hint: The cleverest: which kind of the?
exercises.feedback: A superlative needs the definite article, agreeing with the noun.
exercises.explanation: Aluna is feminine, so the cleverest pupil is a aluna mais inteligente.

answers: uma
mistakes.why: Uma means a, one of many. A superlative picks out the single top one.

answers: o
mistakes.why: That is the masculine article, and aluna is feminine.

exercises.instruction: Write the word for of the.
exercises.source: Hoje é o dia mais quente ____ ano.
answers: do
exercises.feedback: Ano is masculine, so de joins o.
exercises.explanation: O dia mais quente do ano: the hottest day of the year.

answers: da
mistakes.why: That is de + a, for a feminine noun; ano is masculine.

answers: no
mistakes.why: No means in the; after a superlative Portuguese uses of the.

answers: de
mistakes.why: De alone leaves out the article that ano needs here.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Portuguese.
exercises.source: It is the best restaurant in the city.
answers: É o melhor restaurante da cidade.
Este é o melhor restaurante da cidade.
Esse é o melhor restaurante da cidade.
exercises.feedback: The best is o melhor, and in the city is da cidade.
exercises.explanation: O melhor restaurante da cidade: the irregular form with the article makes the superlative.

answers: É o restaurante mais bom da cidade.
É o mais bom restaurante da cidade.
mistakes.why: Bom never takes mais, even in the superlative.

answers: É o melhor restaurante na cidade.
mistakes.why: After a superlative, in the becomes of the in Portuguese.

answers: É melhor restaurante da cidade.
mistakes.why: Without the article it means better, not the best.

exercises.instruction: Build the sentence: This is the biggest bedroom in the house. Leave two tiles unused.
exercises.source: This is the biggest bedroom in the house.
answers: Este é o maior quarto da casa.
Este é o quarto maior da casa.
exercises.feedback: Grande uses its irregular form in the superlative too.
exercises.explanation: O maior quarto da casa: the article turns maior into the biggest.

answers: Este é o mais grande quarto da casa.
Este é o quarto mais grande da casa.
mistakes.why: Grande never takes mais; leave both of those tiles unused.

exercises.instruction: Fix the error.
exercises.source: Este é o filme mais bom do ano.
answers: Este é o melhor filme do ano.
exercises.feedback: The best is a single word with the article.
exercises.explanation: O melhor filme do ano: melhor usually stands before the noun.

answers: Este é o filme mais bom do ano.
mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged: bom does not take mais.

answers: Este é o filme bom do ano.
mistakes.why: Without a comparison word it only says good, not the best.

exercises.instruction: Choose the word for very good.
exercises.source: A comida está ____.
answers: ótima
exercises.hint: One word already means very good; then check the gender.
exercises.feedback: Ótimo already means very good, and it agrees with comida.
exercises.explanation: Comida is feminine, so very good is ótima. Muito bom would also be right.

answers: muito ótima
mistakes.why: This word already means very good, so muito in front doubles it.

answers: ótimo
mistakes.why: That is the masculine form; comida is feminine.

exercises.instruction: Write the one word for very beautiful.
exercises.source: Esta praia é ____ (linda).
answers: lindíssima
exercises.hint: Drop the final vowel and add -íssima.
exercises.feedback: Linda + -íssima: very beautiful in one word.
exercises.explanation: Linda loses its -a and takes -íssima: esta praia é lindíssima.

answers: lindíssimo
mistakes.why: The ending must agree with praia, which is feminine.

answers: muito lindíssima
mistakes.why: The -íssima ending already means very; muito doubles it.

answers: lindaíssima
mistakes.why: The final vowel drops before the ending is added.

exercises.instruction: Replace muito + adjective with one word in -íssimo.
exercises.source: O hotel é muito caro.
answers: O hotel é caríssimo.
exercises.feedback: Drop the final -o and add -íssimo.
exercises.explanation: Caro becomes caríssimo: very expensive in one word.

answers: O hotel é muito caríssimo.
mistakes.why: The ending already means very; muito must go.

answers: O hotel é caroíssimo.
mistakes.why: The final vowel drops before the ending is added.

answers: O hotel é caríssima.
mistakes.why: Hotel is masculine, so the ending stays masculine.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Portuguese.
exercises.source: The dinner was very good.
answers: O jantar estava muito bom.
O jantar estava ótimo.
O jantar foi muito bom.
O jantar foi ótimo.
exercises.feedback: Very good is muito bom or ótimo, never muito ótimo.
exercises.explanation: O jantar estava ótimo or muito bom. Brazilians rarely say boníssimo; ótimo is the everyday one-word form.

answers: O jantar estava muito ótimo.
O jantar foi muito ótimo.
mistakes.why: Ótimo already means very good; muito doubles it.

answers: O jantar estava melhor.
O jantar foi melhor.
mistakes.why: Melhor means better, a comparison with something else.

exercises.instruction: Fix the error.
exercises.source: O café está muito ótimo.
answers: O café está ótimo.
O café está muito bom.
exercises.feedback: Ótimo already means very good.
exercises.explanation: Say o café está ótimo, or o café está muito bom.

answers: O café está muito ótimo.
mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged: muito plus a word that already means very good.

answers: O café está muito ótima.
O café está ótima.
mistakes.why: Café is masculine, so the adjective stays masculine.

exercises.instruction: Choose the right form of tall.
exercises.source: Minhas irmãs são mais ____ do que eu.
answers: altas
exercises.feedback: The adjective agrees with the subject, not with eu.
exercises.explanation: Irmãs is feminine plural, so tall is altas, whatever follows do que.

answers: alto
mistakes.why: The masculine singular matches neither the gender nor the number of irmãs.

answers: alta
mistakes.why: Feminine is right, but irmãs is plural.

answers: altos
mistakes.why: Plural is right, but irmãs is feminine.

exercises.instruction: Write pequeno in the right form.
exercises.source: A cozinha é menos ____ do que a sala.
answers: pequena
exercises.feedback: With menos the adjective keeps its own form and agrees with the subject.
exercises.explanation: A cozinha is feminine singular, so small is pequena.

answers: pequeno
mistakes.why: The masculine form does not match cozinha.

answers: menor
mistakes.why: That replaces mais pequeno, and menos is already in the sentence.

exercises.instruction: Fix the error.
exercises.source: As praias aqui são mais bonito do que lá.
answers: As praias aqui são mais bonitas do que lá.
As praias aqui são mais bonitas que lá.
exercises.feedback: The adjective agrees with praias.
exercises.explanation: Praias is feminine plural, so pretty is bonitas.

answers: As praias aqui são mais bonito do que lá.
mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged: the adjective does not agree with praias.

answers: As praias aqui são mais bonita do que lá.
mistakes.why: Feminine now, but praias is plural.

exercises.instruction: Replace O hotel with As casas and make everything agree.
exercises.source: O hotel é tão caro quanto o apartamento.
answers: As casas são tão caras quanto o apartamento.
As casas são tão caras como o apartamento.
exercises.hint: Verb and adjective follow the new subject; tão never changes.
exercises.feedback: Change ser and the adjective; leave tão and quanto as they are.
exercises.explanation: As casas são tão caras quanto o apartamento: são for plural, caras for feminine plural.

answers: As casas são tão caro quanto o apartamento.
mistakes.why: The adjective still matches o hotel, not the new subject.

answers: As casas é tão caras quanto o apartamento.
mistakes.why: The verb must be plural for several houses.

answers: As casas são tantas caras quanto o apartamento.
mistakes.why: The word before the adjective never agrees; only the noun form does.

exercises.instruction: Choose the word for bigger.
exercises.source: Estas cidades são ____ do que a minha.
answers: maiores
exercises.feedback: Maior has a plural in -es.
exercises.explanation: Maior, melhor, pior and menor do not change for gender but add -es in the plural: maiores.

answers: maior
mistakes.why: Cidades is plural, and the comparative must be plural too.

answers: mais grandes
mistakes.why: Grande never takes mais, plural or not.
